# PR #3691: Patch: the living board's standing scene costs a phone less a frame: diorama slices and face-down backs animate on composited layers

Part of #3674

This cuts the idle living board's per-frame cost and lets the effects director shed within a slow moment. **It does not meet the issue's acceptance: `fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx` still fails 3 of 4.** The Anomaly cast improved and passed once at 360x780. The Mythic takeover, reached on that run, still misses badly (79.0 ms mean / 245 ms worst at best), as the plan's open question 1 predicted. Its cost is long React commits, not the standing scene, so it needs its own follow-up issue, which a person must open (I have no GitHub access). Until then the daily super run's `e2e component (chrome)` stays red.

## What changed

- **Board Mythics' diorama slices are lifted** (`apps/web/src/cards/art/dioramas/lift.ts`, `CardArt.tsx`, `artLive.css`).
  - Which slices: one whose motion is a single chain of loops around everything it draws, by moves whose origin the page can name.
  - How they draw: the slice's still picture, byte for byte the slice less its motion style, sits on HTML layers, one per loop.
  - What moves them: `cf-lift-*` keyframes in `artLive.css`, each one of `ART_MOVES` with picture units as percents. The compositor runs them, so a frame restyles none of the picture's SVG groups.
  - How many: 115 of the 378 slices across all dioramas.
- **The face-down breath drops its `filter`** (`facedown.css`). It now animates `scale` only. Its brightening is a `::before` overlay of 8% white that animates opacity on the same 4.8 s beat, from the same single face-down rule (R2111000).
- **A shed step re-renders only what it changes.**
  - Faces (`motionSlots.ts`) read only whether the stage stills faces.
  - Tile auras (`TileAura.tsx`) read only the aura scale.
  - The aura layer (`AuraLayer.tsx`) reads the aura scale and the set of auras under the pointer. A pointer moving inside the same auras costs no re-render and no forced layout.
- **R3674000 (amends R3606000):** every run of `FX_ADAPT_MOMENT_WINDOW` (8) frames, counted from each window's start, whose mean passes `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` sheds one stage deeper, on every viewport. The particle cap stays the slow window's alone, and a run and a window that end on the same frame shed one stage between them.
- **The rest:** ruling note and `spec/pending/3674.md`; `lift.test.ts` added to R3351000's `proven_in`; a `visual: true` fragment `the-living-board-s-standing-scene-costs-a-phone-less-a-frame.json`; a paragraph in `ART.md`.

No budget, throttle, `FRAME_ATTEMPTS`, moment, layer, beat, hold or timing changed. No Rust changed.

## Measurements

`fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx`, Chrome, 4x throttling. Rows are mean / worst frame in ms for attempts 1 / 2 / 3; the budget is 50 / 120. The base runs used a separate worktree at `13bd66f`. A size stops at its first moment that fails, so the takeover was reached only once.

| Run | Size | Anomaly cast | Mythic takeover |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, base | 390x844 | 80.8/235, 72.6/192, 63.4/120 | not reached |
| 1, base | 360x780 | 113.0/272, 60.6/115, 59.2/142 | not reached |
| 1, base | 844x390 | 76.9/202, 64.7/161, 64.3/183 | not reached |
| 1, this branch | 390x844 | 80.4/273, 51.7/82, 55.4/80 | not reached |
| 1, this branch | 360x780 | 96.1/324, 54.4/152, 54.2/126 | not reached |
| 1, this branch | 844x390 | 82.9/202, 63.3/143, 74.5/148 | not reached |
| 2, base | 390x844 | 101.9/256, 69.0/135, 54.7/82 | not reached |
| 2, base | 360x780 | 79.6/276, 56.0/147, 62.5/135 | not reached |
| 2, base | 844x390 | 85.3/296, 62.9/141, 60.2/149 | not reached |
| 2, this branch | 390x844 | 81.8/277, 53.6/124, 51.2/85 | not reached |
| 2, this branch | 360x780 | 89.3/271, **48.5/104 (passes)** | **108.5/345, 82.3/240, 79.0/245 (fails)** |
| 2, this branch | 844x390 | 79.4/246, 58.2/153, 64.2/159 | not reached |

The forced-shed test passed in every run.

Moments still over 50 / 120:
- the Anomaly cast at 390x844 and 844x390;
- the Mythic takeover at 360x780, the only size where it was reached.

## How it was tested

- **Web suite:** the full suite first had 4 failures among 12,777 tests: 3 in `src/motion.test.ts` (#2110's ledger of stylesheet times and curves) and 1 in `artLive.test.tsx` (this sheet may not use `transform`). Both are fixed (see decisions below). The touched tests, every stylesheet scanner, `src/cards/art` and `src/fx` then passed: 151 files, 2,507 tests.
- **Harness web command** (`vitest run --project web --changed origin/main …`): 401 files, 7,817 passed, 111 skipped. I added no skips.
- **Each new test fails on the base code:**
  - the three re-render tests (faces, tile aura, aura layer);
  - the three R3674000 director tests.
  - The overlapping-auras test passes on both by design, since it pins behavior that must not change.
- **Other checks, all passing:** `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck:component`, eslint on every changed file, `cargo fmt --check`, `jackioh catalog check`, `patches check`, `spec check`.
- **`jackioh classify --claims`:** "Cards, micro: how cards look changed". I ran it on a throwaway commit object built from a temporary index, so neither the branch nor the real index changed.
- **Component specs in Chrome, all passing:** art-answers, card-cosmetics, card-depth, card-diorama, card-faces, card-versions, classic-scenes, classicplus-scenes, core-scenes, full-art-board, card-fullscreen, aura-layer and tile-aura (395 tests), and fx-phone-frame alone (30 tests).
- **Look:** the art-answers screenshots of the board Mythic are the same picture on base and this branch; only the loops' phase differs.
- **Not run locally:** `cargo clippy` and `cargo test`, since no Rust changed.

## Decisions the plan did not settle, or where I departed from it

- **The farthest slice is never lifted**, so I dropped the plan's base-window lift and `.cf-art-shade`. None of the 378 farthest slices can lift, because each holds the sky beside pieces of other roles. `lift.test.ts` pins that.
- **The aura layer counts every aura under the pointer, not just the first.** The plan's `nearAura` named only the first box. Auras overlap (board, side, lane), and before this change each one under the pointer kept its whole budget; a test pins that.
- **The moment run restarts with each window.** The plan's test (7 slow frames shed nothing, the 8th sheds) only holds then. The alternative, a free-running counter, would have left runs misaligned after a window.
- **The lift keyframes use `translate`/`rotate`/`scale`, not `transform`**, because `artLive.test.tsx` holds that sheet to those properties. A scale written before a translate becomes a translate scaled by the same factor (drift's ±1.5 becomes ±1.59), which draws the same thing. `lift.test.ts` derives the expected CSS from `ART_MOVES`.
- **The lift curves are `var(--ease-in-out)`, not the bare `ease-in-out` keyword**, because #2110 forbids a sheet gaining curves of its own. The control points differ by 0.03, which can't be seen on loops of 2–12 s. The rejected option was adding 8 untokened curves to the ledger.
- **`motion.test.ts`'s ledger lists the glow loop**: `KEEP` and `ANIM_SCALED` now include `facedown.css`'s second 4.8 s loop.
- **`liftSvg` also requires a 100-unit square picture.** Percents equal picture units only there; every painter's picture is that size today.
- **The plan's other limits stand:** hero portrait motes, tile motes, live (non-diorama) faces and hand depth planes are unchanged.

## Worth a second look

- **Edge slivers.** A lifted layer draws its picture clipped to the 100-unit square. Content an SVG draws past its own edge could show a sliver of 1.5–2.5% at the window's longer edge during bob, hop, float or sway. I saw nothing like that in the screenshots.
- **`container-type: size`** on a lifted `.cf-art` makes it a stacking context. The art-answers specs (hover, press, attack swing) pass.
- **One slip:** I ran `git fetch --dry-run` once, which reached GitHub read-only and updated no ref.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `claude-7`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 10 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 7s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 154s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 2s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 3s |
| clippy (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`) | pass | 170s |
| cargo tests (`cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts && test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- apps/web/src/wire)"`) | pass | 1787s |
| web tests (`sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts'`) | pass | 1138s |
